hail: Brandt, you on? I’ve got a local pull for you when you’re ready.
angie_call: Angie Kraemer slid off County K. West ditch, just south of Saint Hedwig's.
bridge_call: Taped sedan on Highway sixty-four, at the east end of the river bridge. Take it to storage.
farm_call: Lindquist place on Kolpack. Gary went to check heifers and put two wheels in the ditch. Again.
dairy_call: Hazard on Hendricks Road, east of County K. Taped and checked. Bring it to your yard.
hold_call: Need you on Swamp Road at the Section Three corner. County vehicle. Kowalski's out there.
angie_dir: Out your gate, right on K. Cross Main. Look for the twin steeples, then the car in the west ditch.
bridge_dir: Take K south to Main. Turn right on sixty-four and stay on it to the river bridge.
farm_dir: East on sixty-four to Kolpack, then south. Look for the Lindquist silo on the east side.
dairy_dir: County K south past the church. Left at Hendricks. The car's on the north shoulder.
hold_dir: North on County K to the ginseng frames. Right on Swamp Road. Kowalski is at the section corner.
yard_dir: Brandt yard, west side of K, just north of Main. Bring the truck through the east gate.
storage_dir: Brandt yard, west side of K. Bear right inside the gate to the amber lights at STORAGE.
evidence_dir: Brandt yard, west side of K. Bear left by the office. Back the pickup into the amber-lit EVIDENCE HOLD bay.
angie: My tires were on the white line. I could see the steeples the whole time. Thank you for coming.
gary: Bev said the heifers could wait till morning. You can tell her I was already on my way back.
deputy: Hold for investigation. Tripod goes with it. Lock it up. Don't go through it.
plow: Garage, I’m going to sit here a minute.
clear: Copy that, Brandt. I'll be on the air.
can: County plow's bringing a can. You owe Duane a coffee.
student_call: A student slid off County K near the twin steeples. West side again. There's room for a pull.
student: I thought the headlights behind me were another car. Turned out it was the church windows.
rural_call: Got a driver stuck off Kolpack by the Lindquist place. Easy to find the silo. Harder to find the pavement.
rural: The plow went by just before you did. Took the loose snow off my hood. Thank you.
river_call: There's another checked car at the Highway sixty-four bridge. East shoulder. Standard storage.
milk_call: Dairy called in a car sticking into Hendricks. Deputy checked it. Haul it in when you're ready.
student_pull: Dad told me to stay put and run the heater. I’ve still got half a tank.
dairy_hand: They're holding a spot for me on the next milking. Thanks for coming out.
shift_worker: I work nights. Usually the plow's already been through by the time I head in.
aide_pull: Mrs. Buresh saw me go in from her kitchen. She'll still be at the window. Give her a wave when you go by.
baker_pull: First batch of rye is rising on the counter. If it's halfway to the ceiling when I get there, you'll know whose fault it was.
mechanic_pull: My tools are still in the trunk. That thump was my socket set. Does it every time I take a corner.
boiler_pull: My relief's sitting by the gauges with his coat on. He'll tell me to take my time. He'll have his lunchbox packed, too.
relief_pull: My good scraper's in my other coat. Tried to clear that blade with a feed-store calendar. You can guess how well that worked.
custodian_pull: School's shut, but somebody's got to open the taps in the locker room. Coldest pipes in that building.
nurse_pull: My badge is in my lunch bag. If the hospital calls looking for me, tell them I'm on my way.
plow_shop: Garage, put a passenger-side wiper blade on the counter for me. I'll pick it up on my way in.
duane_ditch: Had my eye on something over the field. There's still a load of salt in the box. Rear eye's clear.
duane_windrow: Blade found the soft shoulder before my tires did. Get me back on the crown and I'll take it from there.
ems_handoff: We got him through the night doors. Kit’s got the empty cot. Give her a shout at the back and she’ll roll it inside.
pelz_pull: I got the flares out for a jackknifed trailer. They got it straightened up and here I am.
ruiz_pull: Backed up to read a plate. Rear wheels dropped right off the edge. My relief's waiting on this car.
freight_lights: I've been sitting up there watching those three lights. They haven't moved an inch. Folks at River Lanes said to use their pull-through.
freight_brake: Trailer tried to pass me on the right. Box is still sealed. The mechanic at River Lanes has a set of air lines waiting.
freight_dir: Stay on US 59 to River Lanes by Highway 64. Take the open apron beside the diner. Pull the tractor and trailer straight between the four amber posts.
milk_herd: Seal number’s on the pump door. I heard the shaft go as I pulled out. Lights went out at the barn before that. Whole herd stood outside in the snow.
milk_haul: Part of a load in there. You’ll feel it come ahead when you brake. Relief truck’s meeting me at Brzezinski. Check that seal at the back before you pull.
milk_dir: Brzezinski Dairy on Hendricks, just east of K. Use the apron under the milk house light. Ease off before the turns and brake early. Put the tank inside the four posts.
displaced_driver: I was on the four-lane outside Wausau. Where am I?
gentle_driver: It picked the whole car up. Set it down real gentle.
lost_hours: I pulled over to look. Ten minutes, tops. The clock on the dash says three hours.
summer_driver: It was warm where I was. Could you drop me at the Fuel & Food?
bev_heifers: The heifers have been standing like that since supper.
mai_lot: Lot lights went out at ten after two again.
angie_sunburn: Third sunburn this week. In January.
arlene_log: Got another one over Swamp Road. Lights, no action.
gary_heifers: Bev says they’ve been standing in that circle since supper. Hasn’t lost one yet.
